## Why This Is Asked

```javascript
// Lightweight snippet to compute per-tenant IOPS targets

  return Math.max(1, Math.floor(share));
}
```

## Why This Question Is Asked

This question assesses practical, beginner-friendly problem-solving skills for real-world I/O contention in multi-tenant Linux environments. It evaluates the ability to implement measurable fixes, maintain safe rollback procedures, and use standard tooling instead of ad-hoc solutions.

## Key Concepts

- **cgroups v2 blkio.weight**: Provides per-tenant I/O budgeting to prevent any single container from monopolizing disk resources
- **I/O Schedulers (BFQ vs. CFQ)**: Control how the kernel queues and dispatches I/O requests, directly impacting tail latency for bursty workloads. BFQ excels at low-latency, interactive I/O, while CFQ offers balanced throughput for mixed workloads on SSDs
- **fio**: A flexible I/O testing tool used to establish baseline metrics and validate performance improvements after configuration changes

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates practical expertise in real-time Linux systems engineering, specifically CPU isolation, interrupt management, and deterministic scheduling under load. It assesses a candidate's ability to design hardware topology-aware solutions that guarantee audio processing latency requirements.

## Key Concepts
- CPU isolation with isolcpus and nohz_full for deterministic execution
- IRQ affinity management and irqbalance service control
- cgroups v2 hierarchy with dedicated real-time slices
- SCHED_FIFO real-time scheduler with priority management
- Memory locking strategies for preventing cache misses and swapping
- Performance validation using cyclictest and synthetic workloads

## Code Example
```bash
# GRUB configuration for CPU isolation
GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX="isolcpus=4-7 nohz_full=4-7"

# Systemd rt.slice configuration
[Slice]
CPUQuota=100%
CPUAffinity=4 5 6 7
MemoryAccounting=yes
MemoryLimit=infinity

# Real-time service configuration
[Service]
Slice=rt.slice
CPUSchedulingPolicy=fifo
CPUSchedulingPriority=99
LimitMEMLOCK=infinity
```

## Why This Is Asked
Security-critical deployments require verifiable runtime integrity. This tests knowledge of kernel integrity (IMA), secure deployment workflows, and integration with systemd and CI.

## Key Concepts
- Linux IMA and runtime attestation
- Signed binaries in CI and secure repositories
- systemd integration (ExecStartPre) and rollback mechanisms
- Tamper-detection tests and observability

## Code Example
```bash
# validate-binaries.sh (conceptual)
set -euo pipefail
EXPECTED_HASH=$(cat /etc/ci/signatures/service.sha256)
ACTUAL_HASH=$(sha256sum /usr/local/bin/myservice | awk '{print $1}')
if [ "$ACTUAL_HASH" != "$EXPECTED_HASH" ]; then
  echo "Signature mismatch" >&2
  exit 1
fi
```

```ini
# /etc/systemd/system/myservice.service (snippet)
[Unit]
Description=My Critical Service

[Service]
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/myservice
ExecStartPre=/usr/local/bin/validate-binaries.sh
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle CI/CD with multiple binary variants across environments?
- How would you monitor and alert on attestation failures in production?

## Why This Is Asked
Multi-tenant logging can cause IO contention and latency spikes when many small writers share a single path. This question tests practical isolation, rotation, and QoS strategies without changing app code.

## Key Concepts
- Systemd sandboxing: PrivateTmp, PrivateDevices, ReadOnlyPaths
- Per-tenant log isolation and rotation using logrotate
- Disk I/O control: ionice and IO scheduling
- Quotas: per-tenant quotas on a dedicated log volume (e.g., project quotas on XFS)
- Test plan: simulate bursts and verify rollback safety

## Code Example
```ini
; /etc/systemd/system/ci-agent@.service
[Unit]
Description=CI Agent for tenant %i

[Service]
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/ci-agent --tenant=%i
PrivateTmp=true
PrivateDevices=true
ReadOnlyPaths=/var/log/ci
AmbientCapabilities=CAP_SYSLOG
IOSchedulingClass=idle
IOSchedulingPriority=7
```

```bash
; /etc/logrotate.d/ci-agent-%i
/var/log/ci/tenant-*/agent.log {
  size 50M
  rotate 7
  copytruncate
  missingok
  notifempty
}
```

- Which metrics would you monitor to detect drift or misconfigurations, and how would you roll back safely?
